correspondence.component_scope: Headward opening and northern turn
correspondence.finding: The selected opening and complete northward-to-eastward arch lie in the original map’s Inland Ice west of the Camp Century setting. The blue ice coverage and contour pattern expose the full first two stored parts, including the northernmost turn. No named river or surveyed watercourse follows this entire selected arch in the inspected source. Camp Century is a locality-context label only.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward continuation across Inland Ice
correspondence.finding: Every small stored part of the eastward continuation is within the same continuous mapped Inland Ice area, approaching the sector southwest of the Camp Century label. The original covers the small part joins and their surrounding ice terrain at ordinary regional scale. Surface contours, dashed ice-thickness isopachs and underlying-bedrock contours are distinguished from river channels; their crossings do not demonstrate water flow.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastward succession and intermediate joins
correspondence.finding: The complete succession of short southeastward stored parts remains in mapped Inland Ice southwest of Camp Century and inland of Lauge Koch Kyst. The contiguous original cartography exposes this whole interval and its joins with the eastern incoming sequence and the following bends. It supplies terrain correspondence, not evidence of a continuous surface or subglacial river.

correspondence.component_scope: Small lower-ice bends and southward departure
correspondence.finding: The series of small bends and subsequent southward departure are wholly covered in the mapped lower Inland Ice. The nearby label and contours provide ordinary geographical orientation but no natural-river name or hydraulic connection. Every stored bend, including the short reverse turns, is accounted for at source scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward approach toward Lauge Koch Kyst
correspondence.finding: The southward parts move through the lower ice-margin sector toward the exposed-rock coastal belt labelled Lauge Koch Kyst. The original shows the ice/rock and coastal-island pattern across the complete approach, rather than leaving the lower end at an inland label. There is no established named river reach, lake connector, managed channel or reservoir connector in this selected approach.

correspondence.component_scope: Final stored part and actual selected terminal
correspondence.finding: The entire final stored part, including its long southward segment and final endpoint, is covered by the original’s ice-margin, exposed-rock and coastal-water setting along Lauge Koch Kyst on the Melville Bugt side. The actual rendered endpoint and stored source endpoint belong to that same generalized terminal setting. This is correspondence to the selected final position, not a substitution of an upstream point or a nearby bay label. The national map’s scale and historical epoch do not justify an exact present land/ice/water boundary, a specific glacier or small embayment assignment, or an ordinary natural-river mouth claim.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected headward opening and East Fork Chehalis River approach
correspondence.finding: The detailed original places the selected opening north of Elochoman Pass on the mapped East Fork Chehalis River. The route follows the eastward then northward valley and turns northwest past the eastern tributary entries, including the mapped Clintapax Creek junction. No claim is made that this selected opening is the natural river source.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Supported at ordinary headward-valley and junction scale; small modeled bend shortcuts do not establish exact banks.

correspondence.component_scope: East/West Fork union and upper Chehalis valley
correspondence.finding: The detailed original depicts East Fork joining West Fork and the receiving channel labeled Chehalis River continuing north. The upper original follows that valley through the tributary settings of Thrash Creek, Smith Creek, the Pe Ell approach and Elk Creek to the eastward turn. The supplied route follows the receiving valley rather than treating West Fork or the side streams as selected continuations.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Supported upper receiving corridor and fork union.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward upper valley and South Fork junction toward Chehalis
correspondence.finding: The upper original maps the selected eastward corridor beside the Route 6/Ludinghaus Road setting, the receiving bend near Ceres Hill, the entry of South Fork Chehalis River, and the Chehalis continuation toward the city. South Fork is a separately named incoming branch; it is not assigned the main candidate name as a scalar reach.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Supported valley bends and actual South Fork entry.

correspondence.component_scope: Chehalis–Centralia, Grand Mound, Black River and Oakville transition
correspondence.finding: The upper original follows the northward Chehalis corridor beside Chehalis and Centralia, including the eastern Skookumchuck River entry, then west around Grand Mound and the Chehalis Reservation. The Black River junction is mapped north of the westward corridor. Overlapping upper and lower originals carry the selected route across the 9461/9462 fragment transition and into the Oakville northward turn.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Supported receiving corridor, lateral entries and inter-fragment continuity at ordinary scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Oakville–Porter–Elma corridor and Satsop entry
correspondence.finding: The lower original maps the selected northwestward Chehalis valley through the Oakville/Porter corridor and the broad Elma floodplain. Its westward continuation receives Satsop River. Moores Lake and Huttula Lake are shown beside this plain; the selected route corresponds to the Chehalis receiving corridor south of their settings, and no independent through-lake connection is imposed.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Supported main-valley route and Satsop junction, distinct from nearby lakes and side channels.

correspondence.component_scope: Brady–Montesano, Wynoochee entry and lower Chehalis/slough plain
correspondence.finding: The lower original follows the Chehalis west through Brady and the Montesano plain, depicts the Wynoochee River entry, and maps the continued lower river across the 9462/9463 transition. The selected receiving corridor passes the extensive Willow, Preachers and Blue slough settings toward Cosmopolis and the east side of Aberdeen. Named sloughs and wetland branches remain distinct; map coverage is not used to assign every such channel the same name.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Supported lower receiving corridor and inter-fragment link; precise tidal-channel centerlines and individual bend cuts are outside scope.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected Aberdeen terminal
correspondence.finding: Both the lower original and the detailed terminal original show the Chehalis River bending west and southwest through Aberdeen Reach. The last selected segment instead runs southwest from the mapped river across the South Aberdeen street/landward setting and ends in the West Huntley Street area. The detailed original does not depict a waterway following that final selected segment to its actual endpoint. Neither the surrounding Chehalis identity nor the nearby estuarine water establishes this link.
correspondence.coverage_limit: Material terminal-connection gap. The actual selected end is not replaced with a more convenient river mouth or a Grays Harbor endpoint.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected eastern opening and initial lake-and-channel chain
correspondence.finding: The supplied opening lies east of the airborne survey footprint. The original report overview includes this broad area but does not establish the small opening waterbody, its exit or each transfer into the northward upper reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper northward bend and northwestward approach
correspondence.finding: The report’s generalized hydrographic background places the corridor among the eastern lake country. It is a sheet-index figure, and no detailed original demonstrates every selected lake entry, exit and intervening join.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle approach, northward bend and westward continuation
correspondence.finding: The selected middle passage crosses the mapped regional lake-and-channel country. The source index labels 34N06 Rivière Polemond as a map-sheet title, not as a proved name of this complete selected route. The actual selected through-links remain unresolved.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower northwestward chain and joining corridors
correspondence.finding: The northwestward lower passage is north of the airborne survey footprint. The sparse report background does not establish all selected lake transfers or the identity and connectivity of adjoining channels.

correspondence.component_scope: Last lake/channel passage and actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The selected final passage is near the top edge of the generalized overview and outside the survey footprint. The exact selected coastal connection is not established. Neither the unavailable nesting-study map nor the denied expedition publication supplies terminal evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Managed, wetland and glacier connectors
correspondence.finding: No specific managed or glacier connector is positively identified in inspected material. The report overview cannot prove or exclude small wetland or seasonal connections along the selected chain.

correspondence.component_scope: headward opening
correspondence.finding: The selected headward opening and descent toward the regional western plain have no inspected original map correspondence. A nearby or basin-level name cannot settle the opening.

correspondence.component_scope: upper, middle and lower river course
correspondence.finding: All50 supplied mainstem parts remain without substantive map correspondence, including their intermediate joins and any distinct local reach identity. Fundación remains an unverified discovery lead only.

correspondence.component_scope: fragment transition and waterbody entrance
correspondence.finding: The shared supplied endpoint is known from the selected path; the geographical river-to-lagoon/wetland transfer has no inspected source confirmation.

correspondence.component_scope: lagoon/wetland through-link
correspondence.finding: The long northward then northeastward selected continuation cannot be treated as a named river or confirmed lagoon flow path from source membership or a broad wetland label.

correspondence.component_scope: actual terminal and sea connection
correspondence.finding: The selected endpoint must be matched to the actual coastal opening with independent ordinary corridor evidence. The supplied sea classification and likely Boca de la Barra setting do not independently establish that connection.

correspondence.component_scope: tributary, managed or other connectors
correspondence.finding: No additional tributary-role fragment is selected. The absence or presence of managed canals, barriers or local waterbody transitions along the selected mainstem cannot be inferred without original mapping.
